title: Why Do Atoms Shrink? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
An onion grows with every new layer, and a magnet pulls paper clips in tight. Atoms follow the same two rules: more shells make them bigger, and a stronger pull from the nucleus makes them smaller. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) Diya peels an onion and we find out why a fluorine atom is smaller than a lithium atom.

You will see how atomic size is measured (covalent radius and metallic radius, half the distance between nuclei), then watch the atoms of period 2 shrink live on the molecule bench from Li 152 pm to F 64 pm as protons are added to the same shell, and grow down group 1 from Li 152 pm to Cs 262 pm as new shells are added (NCERT Table 3.6). Sodium loses an electron and drops from 186 to 95 pm; fluorine gains one and grows from 64 to 136 pm. Then we rank isoelectronic ions (O2-, F-, Na+, Mg2+) step by step, work out the radii of chlorine (99 pm) and copper (128 pm), meet the exam trap, and solve an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 31 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Layers versus pull
0:28 Covalent and metallic radius
0:54 Across period 2: atoms shrink
1:30 Down group 1: atoms grow
1:44 Ions: Na+ shrinks, F- grows
2:15 Pause and think: F- or Na+?
2:31 Isoelectronic ions, step by step
3:12 Worked example: Cl and Cu radii
3:49 Exam trap: same electrons, same size?
4:14 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:53 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Ionization Enthalpy. Why does it take more energy to pull an electron from fluorine than from lithium?
